equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest (25% of e&s) at book

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Revenue 5yr CAGR (4.4%) tempered to 3.5%: equity CAGR (4.7%) understates the earnings engine because the payout ratio is ~90%, while the 10yr revenue CAGR (10.8%) is inflated by the FY2017 Good Guys acquisition. 3.5% is roughly AU population growth plus CPI with modest share gain.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR -2.2% vs equity 3yr CAGR +5.0% (>30% divergence): FY2023 was the post-COVID earnings peak (EPS $4.78) and FY2026 EPS ($4.47) is still 6.5% below it. Growth since FY2021 has been revenue-led with margin give-back, not margin-led.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (treatment B: ex lease principal, SBC and interest income) are below reported-FCF CAGRs on both horizons (-4.9% vs -1.6% 3yr; 3.8% vs 4.1% 5yr): lease cash is growing ~5%/yr against ~4.5% revenue and FY2025-26 absorbed ~$150m of inventory build. FY2020 owner FCF ($763m) is a COVID working-capital windfall and is excluded from every CAGR base.

scenario_narratives.base: JB Hi-Fi remains the scale leader in Australian consumer electronics with a low-cost, high-turnover model (inventory turns 6.5x, CODB ~15%). FY2027 is a soft year -- the 17 Aug 2026 update showed July comparable sales of -1.4% in JB Australia and -1.7% in The Good Guys, with customers 'increasingly looking for value and migrating their spend to key promotional events' and technology categories held back by supplier price rises and stock availability -- so revenue grows only 1.5% and adj EBITDA slips 15bps. From FY2028 growth reverts to ~3.5% (population + CPI + modest share gain from 4 AU and 2 NZ new stores a year) and margins hold at the FY2026 level. No margin expansion, no re-rating: value is the ~$460-500m/yr of owner FCF the network already produces, capitalised at 14x.
scenario_narratives.bull: A device-replacement cycle (AI PCs, next-gen consoles and handsets) coincides with Australian rate cuts, lifting discretionary spend from FY2028; JB Hi-Fi NZ keeps compounding at 15%+ comps and reaches sustainable mid-single-digit EBIT margins; e&s' premium appliance format scales beyond Victoria; The Good Guys recovers toward its FY2022-23 ~$240m EBIT. Operating leverage on a largely fixed lease and labour base takes adj EBITDA to 9.75% -- still short of the COVID peak -- and the market pays 16x owner FCF for a compounder.
scenario_narratives.bear: The consumer weakness visible in July 2026 is structural rather than cyclical: online pure-plays (Amazon AU, Temu) and vendor direct-to-consumer channels erode JB's technology share, promotional intensity compresses gross margin, and the appliance banners (TGG, e&s) stay in a housing-linked slump. Sales fall 1.5% in FY2027 and grow only 2% thereafter; adj EBITDA reverts to the pre-COVID structure (~8.5%) while rents keep rising against a flat sales base. No solvency question -- zero bank debt and $200m+ cash -- but a 12x exit multiple on shrinking real earnings.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value JB Hi-Fi as a mature cash-generative retailer on fully lease-burdened, SBC-expensed owner FCF (~4.2% of sales normalised), not on post-AASB16 EBITDA. The FY2026 owner FCF of $381m is depressed by a ~$107m inventory/payables outflow; the component build normalises that to ~$460m and grows it with the store network. Leases are an operating cost (treatment B) so the $705m of lease liabilities never appears in net debt; SBC is charged in the flows and the 109.7m share count is held flat. Cyclicality is carried in the bear scenario and a 25% bear weight, with one 9.5% AUD WACC across all scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discretionary demand: July 2026 comps were negative in JB Australia (-1.4%) and The Good Guys (-1.7%); a second consecutive soft year pushes FY2027 toward the bear path.
Channel shift: Amazon Australia and vendor DTC in technology categories; supplier price rises and stock allocation are already cited by management as constraints.
Margin structure: adj EBITDA of 9.25% is ~75bps above the pre-COVID equivalent; the base case assumes it holds rather than reverting.
Lease burden: $249m/yr of lease cash (2.25% of sales) is largely fixed, so operating deleverage on a sales decline is sharp -- the bear case takes lease cost to 2.4% of sales.
Working capital: two consecutive years of inventory build (FY2025 -$44m, FY2026 -$107m); the base case assumes only 5% of incremental revenue is consumed.
Terminal multiple: with margins mature, ~50% of value sits in the terminal; the 14x cap (not Gordon) is what binds in the base case.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (ASX regular close); 52-week range 64.18-120.0.
data_sources.financials: JBH.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2016-FY2026 annual + H1 halves) and the FY2026 annual report (JBH.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt): cash-flow statement lines 5834-5853 (interest received, lease interest, tax paid, capex, lease principal), note 16 leases (lines 6716-6821, ROU depreciation 208.1), note 25 cash-flow reconciliation (lines 6910-6921), EPS note (lines 6067-6086, diluted denominator), balance sheet (lines 5748-5764).
data_sources.qualitative: FY2026 annual report segment review (lines 1313-1420), strategic priorities (lines 1817-1820: 4 AU + 2 NZ new stores FY2027), and the 'Sales update and trading outlook as at 17 August 2026' (lines 1991-2011). JBH.AX_Analysis.json was not yet available at build time.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 109,333,981 shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR note 20) plus 349,255 dilutive options (note, diluted EPS denominator 109.6m weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ~$27m/yr of treasury-share purchases only offsets award vesting.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity / cash-flow reconciliation: share-based payments expense $15.0m (FY2025 $16.6m). No net-share-settlement tax outflow is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year); awards are satisfied from on-market treasury purchases, so the expense line is the full cost.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 $26.9m is on-market purchase of treasury shares to satisfy employee equity awards, not a capital-return buyback. The last true buyback was the $250m off-market buyback in FY2022. Flat count is being funded (repurchaser).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: Australian 10yr government bond ~4.4% + 5.5% AUD equity risk premium x beta ~0.95 for a discretionary retailer with zero bank debt = ~9.6% cost of equity; leases are treated as operating cost (treatment B) so there is no debt in the capital structure and WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the bear flows and the scenario weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B: leases as operating cost. FY2026 lease cash (principal $210.4m financing + interest $38.7m operating = $249.1m, 2.25% of revenue; AR note 16) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and the $705.0m of lease liabilities (208.6 current + 496.4 non-current) is EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation: $273.8m total less $208.1m ROU = $65.7m (0.59% of revenue). Reported OCF/FCF (FY2020+) exclude lease principal, so last_fcf = reported_fcf 613.7 - lease principal 210.4 - SBC 15.0 - interest income 7.1 = 381.2. Pre-AASB16 years (FY2016-19) already carried rent in operating cash flow, so the owner-FCF history is comparable across the change.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: e&s is 75% owned since 2 Sept 2024; NCI book value $4.8m at 30 June 2026 deducted as an equity_bridge item. NCI share of profit was -$0.4m in FY2026 so the flows are effectively attributable already.
inputs.working_capital_note: FY2026 OCF carried a ~$107m working-capital outflow (inventories -65.4, payables -41.2, AR note 25) and FY2025 ~-44m; FY2024 was an inflow. A retailer growing inventory ahead of sales consumes cash, so wc_capture is negative (-5% base of the revenue change, -10% bear, 0 bull). The FY0 component build without that outflow is ~$464m (4.2% of revenue), which is the normalised year-1 anchor.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner-fcf.md + adaptations sections a, b, c, f). JB Hi-Fi is a straightforward operating retailer -- consumer electronics and home appliances across JB Hi-Fi Australia (67% of sales, EBIT $547m), The Good Guys (27%, EBIT $184m), JB Hi-Fi NZ (4%, EBIT $3.5m) and e&s (2.5%, EBIT -$0.4m) -- so the routing table sends it to the owner-FCF DCF with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, IFRS-16 leases, small NCI). Margins are mature: FY2026 adj EBITDA (post-AASB16, pre-SBC) 9.25% sits inside the post-COVID 9.2-10.5% band and above the pre-COVID ~8.5% equivalent, so the 10-year horizon is for the entry-price convention, not a margin ramp. Interest income ($7.1m) is stripped because the $206.5m of cash is added back in the bridge; net cash is below 1x the FCF base so the effect is ~$0.06/share. Analysis JSON was not available at build time (generating in parallel); the bull/bear axes below are drawn from the FY2026 annual report's segment commentary and the 17 Aug 2026 trading update. Price is at the ASX regular close, ~44% below the 52-week high of 120.0 and within 6% of the 52-week low.

bear.growth_rationale: The July 2026 negative comps in the core AU and TGG banners persist through FY2027 (-1.5%) as consumers migrate to promotional events; Amazon and Temu/Shein take share in the technology categories; growth settles at 2%, below CPI.
bear.margin_rationale: Value-seeking mix and promotional intensity compress adj EBITDA to the pre-COVID equivalent of ~8.3-8.5%; rents are fixed so lease cost rises to 2.35-2.4% of a smaller sales base; working capital consumes 10% of each increment.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 1.5%: July 2026 group sales were roughly flat (AU -0.5%, TGG -1.7%, e&s -2.7%, NZ +20.9% on a 4% base) with 6 new stores and supplier price rises adding ~1-2pp through the year. Then 3.5% (population + CPI + share gain) fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Adj EBITDA (post-AASB16, before SBC) dips to 9.10% in FY2027 on negative comps against CODB inflation, then recovers to the FY2026 9.25% and holds; no expansion assumed. Lease cash 2.25-2.27% of sales per FY2024-26 actuals; D&A ex-ROU rises from 0.60% toward the 0.80% capex run-rate less growth capex; cash tax at the 30% statutory rate (FY2026 cash rate 29.3%).
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 14x owner FCF: JBH is a mature, cyclical discretionary retailer that has traded at 10-25x earnings over the decade; 14x FCF is roughly a 15x P/E on the cash-taxed EBIT.

bull.growth_rationale: AI-PC / device-replacement cycle and rate cuts revive Australian discretionary spend from FY2028; NZ keeps compounding at 15%+ off its 28-store base; e&s premium-appliance rollout works. Revenue reaches ~$16bn by FY2036.
bull.margin_rationale: Operating leverage on a fixed lease and labour base lifts adj EBITDA to 9.75% (still below the FY2022-23 COVID 10.5-11%); lease cost drifts to 2.15% of sales as rents lag sales.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25% because the most recent datapoint (July 2026) is negative comparable sales in the two banners that produce 97% of EBIT, and consumer electronics is a discretionary category with a demonstrated 10-25x P/E range across the cycle. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things -- a device cycle, rate cuts and a TGG margin recovery -- to line up. No going-concern or covenant risk argues for a bear weight above 25%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
